Writer fixtures. CLAUDE.md, Working style: fixture before rule — transcribe the source, cite it, then implement until it passes.

EVERY CASE HERE IS CITED TO THE UNICODE CODE CHART OR TO PRD §2, and to nothing else. The dictionary and textbook sources in PRD Appendix A are all PDFs that have not been extracted, so there is not yet a single fixture whose Latin form is attested as a Bugis WORD. These cases test that the engine applies the rule set correctly; they do not claim the strings are Bugis. When the dictionaries are extracted, cited word fixtures go in tests/fixtures/dictionary.fixture.json and reviewer-approved ones in tests/reviewed/.

cases.citation: Unicode code chart U1A00.pdf — U+1A00 BUGINESE LETTER KA carries the inherent vowel /a/.
Unicode code chart U1A00.pdf — U+1A17 BUGINESE VOWEL SIGN I replaces the inherent vowel.
Unicode code chart U1A00.pdf — U+1A18 BUGINESE VOWEL SIGN U.

Attested pairs (data/corpus/bugwiki-pairs.json): plain Latin `e` takes U+1A1B BUGINESE VOWEL SIGN AE, not U+1A19 — Bekasi, Wettu, Peddang, Jeppang, Halaleng and ~25 more. The Unicode character name said otherwise and was wrong.
Unicode code chart U1A00.pdf — U+1A1A BUGINESE VOWEL SIGN O.

Attested pairs (data/corpus/bugwiki-pairs.json): Latin `é` takes U+1A19 BUGINESE VOWEL SIGN E — Sapéda, Sulawési, Baruné, Watamponé, Sawérigading, Éropa. Before rules v0.2.0 `é` was not a vowel at all and the writer silently dropped a whole syllable from `Sapéda`.
Unicode code chart U1A00.pdf — U+1A15 BUGINESE LETTER A carries a vowel with no consonant onset.
Unicode code chart U1A00.pdf — the vowel carrier takes vowel signs like any consonant letter.
PRD §2 — `mata`, `matta` and `manta` are written identically.
PRD §2 — written identically to `mata`. The geminate collapses (lontara.gemination.collapse).

PRD §2 — written identically to `mata`. `nt` is not written by any of the four prenasal letters, and `t` is not the second element of any of them either, so the nasal is classified as a plain unwritten final rather than as prenasalisation. That the classification is narrower than PRD §2's prose suggests is exactly openQuestions.prenasal-coverage.
Derived — inventory.json block.hasVirama = false: no bare consonant can be written, so a word-final consonant is dropped (lontara.final.drop).

PRD §6.7 names the apostrophe in `Lontara'` as how Bugis Latin writes the glottal stop. Nothing in the block writes it, so it is dropped (lontara.glottal.drop). The final `a` of `-ra'` is the inherent vowel of RA. TWO classes are lost, not one: the `n` of `lon-` closes a syllable and is not written either, so NA never appears in the output.
latin.apostrophe.normalize — U+2019 RIGHT SINGLE QUOTATION MARK is normalised to U+0027 before anything else looks at the text. Output identical to glottal.apostrophe, which is the point.
Unicode character name U+1A07 BUGINESE LETTER MPA. The cluster `mp` is written by a single letter, so NOTHING is lost — this is the case that shows prenasalisation is not uniformly unwritten.
Unicode character name U+1A03 BUGINESE LETTER NGKA. Maximal onset takes `ngk` over `ng`, so the cluster is written.
Unicode character name U+1A0B BUGINESE LETTER NRA.
Unicode character name U+1A0F BUGINESE LETTER NYCA.
Unicode character names U+1A02 BUGINESE LETTER NGA and U+1A03 NGKA. `nga` must take NGA, not NGKA — maximal onset tries `ngk` first and it does not match.

Derived — `nk` is not written by any of the four prenasal letters (ngk, mp, nr, nyc), so the nasal is not written (lontara.prenasal.drop). Whether Bugis practice does something else here is openQuestions.prenasal-coverage.
latin.case.fold — every letter in the block is general category Lo with no case mappings, so Latin case carries no information the script can record.
inventory.json takes the onset `w` for U+1A13 from attested pairs (Watangpola, Tawawu, Kuweng, Awayeng, Sulawési); `v` never appears in the corpus. PROVISIONAL — see openQuestions.va-latin.

latin.wa.v, PROVISIONAL — `v` is accepted on input for the same letter, because the Unicode character name BUGINESE LETTER VA leads people to type it. Input tolerance only; the writer never emits `v`.
PRD §2 — a geminate and a glottal stop in one form. Both losses must be declared, each at its own span.

latin.glottal.q, PROVISIONAL — attested pair Goloq → ᨁᨚᨒᨚ. Word-final `q` is not written. Whether it is the glottal stop or a final /k/ changes only the declared class, never the output; see openQuestions.glottal-q.
Attested pair Sapéda → ᨔᨄᨙᨉ. This is the case that exposed `é` being dropped entirely before rules v0.2.0: the output was ᨔᨉ, missing the whole `pé` syllable.
Attested pair Lébarepuluq → ᨒᨙᨅᨑᨛᨄᨘᨒᨘ. Both signs in one word: `é` takes U+1A19 and `e` takes U+1A1B. Plus a word-final `q`.
Attested pair Komputeréq → ᨀᨚᨇᨘᨈᨛᨑᨙ. `mp` written with U+1A07 MPA (so nothing lost there), `e` with U+1A1B, `é` with U+1A19, and a final `q`.
